Subfactors, index and finite-depth classification

Polynomials locate the finite projection gaps

An infinite Jones projection sequence excludes most parameters above . A finite sequence can still exist there. To see how long it can be, we need the exact polynomial normalization and an argument that keeps track of the available generators. We prove both, without assuming a trace or nondegeneracy of the represented algebra.

We use the algebraic projection calculation in Positivity restricts the index, Lemma 7.1, and the joint-kernel interpretation in Why the discrete projection algebra is unique. The proof below supplies the indexing and finite-window calculations explicitly. References are [Jones], [Takesaki] and [Wenzl].

In particular there is no infinite nonzero sequence at such a parameter.

Proof. Every term in a nonzero sequence is nonzero: the adjacent sandwich relations propagate a zero term to all its neighbors. If , the stated bound is immediate. Otherwise Lemmas 42.4–42.5 apply.
